The test image shows a mango shoot/stem with small, deformed, funnel/cone-shaped young leaves at the growing tips — the leaves appear stunted, curled inward, and malformed rather than expanded normally. There is no sooty black coating, no powdery white residue, no canker lesions, and no signs of die-back browning.

This pattern of distorted, curled young leaves clustering at shoot tips is the hallmark signature of **Gall Midge** (*Procontarinia matteiana*) infestation — the larvae feed inside the developing leaf tissue causing characteristic gall-like deformation of the emerging foliage.

The Sooty Mould reference confirms that class shows a blackened coating on mature leaves, which is clearly absent here.
